title: Canned food and botulism
summary: Which cans and jars to throw out, how to sanitize sealed cans after a flood, and botulism warning signs.

sources.title: CDC: Keep Food Safe After a Disaster or Emergency
FDA: Food and Water Safety During Power Outages and Floods

blocks.text: **Botulism is a medical emergency.** If someone has trouble swallowing, double or blurry vision, drooping eyelids, slurred speech, muscle weakness, or trouble breathing after eating suspect food, go to the ER or call 911 right away. **Do not wait.**
Botulism toxin can't be seen, smelled or tasted, and even a tiny taste can be deadly. **Never taste food to check it.**

items: The can or jar is **bulging, swollen, leaking, cracked, or damaged**.
It spurts liquid or foam when you open it.
The food is discolored, moldy, or smells bad.
You don't know whether safe canning steps were followed (home-canned food).
Ready.gov says not to eat from cans that are swollen, dented, or corroded. FDA says swollen, leaking, punctured, deeply rusted or badly dented. **The safe rule: when in doubt, throw it out.**

blocks.text: Difficulty swallowing, muscle weakness, double vision, drooping eyelids, blurry vision, slurred speech, trouble breathing, trouble moving the eyes. Vomiting, nausea, stomach pain and diarrhea can also happen.

Home-canned low-acid foods and home-canned tomatoes are the main risk. If you choose to eat them, CDC says to boil them for **10 minutes** first (at elevations below 1,000 feet, which includes Henrico). Throw them out if the jar or food shows any warning sign above.

Undamaged, commercially canned food in all-metal cans and pouches can be saved. Throw out everything in cardboard, screw-cap jars, snap lids, twist caps and flip tops, plus all home-canned food, if flood or storm water touched it.

items: Remove labels if you can and note the expiration date.
Brush or wipe off dirt and silt.
Sanitize: soak for **15 minutes** in **1 cup of unscented household bleach per 5 gallons of water**, **or** boil the cans for **2 minutes**.
Air dry at least 1 hour. Re-label with a marker, including the expiration date. Use soon.

blocks.text: To heat a can: take the label off, wash the outside, then open it **before** you heat it (Ready.gov).
